title: Study of Global Food Supply
text:
Approach
The project analyzes undernourishment worldwide between 2013 and 2017, as part of a simulated mission within the FAO. The goal is to understand:

global food availability,
resource use,
the distribution of resources between countries,
the role of food aid

title: Study of Global Food Supply
text:
Key Results
The analysis led to the following conclusions:

535.7 million people are undernourished, or 7.1% of the world population
Global food availability would have been enough to feed 7.2 billion people
The countries receiving the most aid are not those with the highest undernourishment rates

Calculating the theoretical number of people who can be fed with plant-based products in Python

text:
Key Deliverables



Relational schema




 Top 3 highest average property values by municipality (departments 06, 13, 33, 59, and 69) (SQL)


SELECT * 
FROM (
    SELECT *,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY join2.Code_departement
            ORDER BY join2.Moyenne_Valeur_Foncière DESC
        ) AS rank
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            c.Nom_commune, 
            c.Code_departement,
            ROUND(AVG(join1.Valeur_fonciere), 2) AS Moyenne_valeur_foncière
        FROM (
            SELECT * 
            FROM Bien b 
            JOIN Vente v ON b.ID_bien = v.ID_bien
        ) join1
        JOIN Commune c 
            ON c.Code_departement_code_commune = join1.COde_departement_code_commune
        WHERE c.Code_departement IN ('06', '13', '33', '59', '69')
        GROUP BY c.Nom_commune
    ) join2
) 
WHERE rank <= 3;

title: Counterfeit Banknote Detection
text:
Approach

Exploratory data analysis


Univariate analysis (distributions, outliers using z-score and IQR)
Multivariate analysis (correlations between variables, Mann-Whitney tests)

Based on this initial analysis, 3 variables appear to be the most discriminating for detecting counterfeit banknotes: bottom margin, top margin and length.

Preprocessing


Train/test split of the dataset (80/20)
Imputation of missing values (mean by banknote type, as less than 2.5% of values were missing)
Data standardization


Model testing


Logistic regression (supervised model)
KNN (supervised model)
Random forest (supervised model)
K-means (unsupervised model)

For each model, results are first analyzed with a confusion matrix (provisional, since the threshold t has not been set at this stage). The best supervised model is then selected by comparing ROC-AUC and PR-AUC scores. This model is tuned by comparing its results at different thresholds t. Finally, it is compared with the unsupervised K-means model using Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1 scores.

Building the application


Export of the full pipeline (preprocessing + model) as a .joblib file
Creation of a .py script that loads the .joblib file
2 ways to use it:

analyze a single banknote by entering its measurements directly
analyze several banknotes from a .csv file

title: Counterfeit Banknote Detection
text:
Key Results
The best supervised model for this project is logistic regression, with a ROC-AUC score of 99.96% and a PR-AUC score of 99.98% on the test set. It also outperforms the unsupervised model (K-means), which achieves accuracy: 99.33%, precision: 99.5%, recall: 99.5% and F1 score: 99.5%.

def predire_plusieurs_billets(pipeline,lien_csv):
    
    with open(lien_csv, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        premiere_ligne = f.readline()
        
    separateur = ';' if ';' in premiere_ligne else ','
    
    X_raw = pd.read_csv(lien_csv, sep=separateur)

    colonnes_attendues = ["diagonal", "height_left", "height_right", "margin_low", "margin_up", "length"]

    X_filled = X_raw.dropna(subset=colonnes_attendues)

    nb_lignes_supp = X_raw.shape[0] - X_filled.shape[0]
    
    if nb_lignes_supp > 0 : 
        print(f"\nAttention : {nb_lignes_supp} billet(s) du fichier csv contienne(nt) des valeurs manquantes. Il n'est pas possible de détecter si ce(s) billet(s) sont vrai(s) ou faux. Il(s) a/ont donc été supprimé(s) du tableau de résultats.\n")

    X = X_filled[colonnes_attendues]

    y = pipeline.predict(X)

    df_resultat = X_filled.copy()
    df_resultat['Résultat_binaire'] = y
    df_resultat['Résultat'] = df_resultat['Résultat_binaire'].map({False : "Faux billet", True : 'Vrai billet'})

    return df_resultat

 Function displaying the projection of individuals

# Function displaying the projection of individuals
def display_factorial_planes(   X_projected, 
                                x_y, 
                                pca=None, 
                                labels = None,
                                clusters=None, 
                                alpha=1,
                                figsize=[10,8], 
                                marker="." ):
    """
    Displays the projection of individuals

    Positional arguments : 
    -------------------------------------
    X_projected : np.array, pd.DataFrame, list of list : matrix of projected points
    x_y : list or tuple : the x,y pair of planes to display, e.g. [0,1] for F1, F2

    Optional arguments :

    labels : list or tuple : labels of the individuals to project, default = None
    clusters : list or tuple : list of the clusters each individual belongs to, default = None
    alpha : float in [0,1] : transparency parameter, 0=100% transparent, 1=0% transparent, default = 1
    figsize : list or tuple : width, height pair defining the figure size in inches, default = [10,8] 
    marker : str : marker type used to represent individuals, dots, crosses, etc., default = "."
    """

    # Convert X_projected to np.array
    X_ = np.array(X_projected)

    # Handle labels
    if  labels is None : 
        labels = []
    try : 
        len(labels)
    except Exception as e : 
        raise e

    # Check the axis variable
    if not len(x_y) ==2 : 
        raise AttributeError("2 axes sont demandées")   
    if max(x_y )>= X_.shape[1] : 
        raise AttributeError("la variable axis n'est pas bonne")   

    # Define x and y
    x, y = x_y

    # Initialize the figure       
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=figsize)

    # Check whether there are clusters
    c = None if clusters is None else clusters
 
    # Points    
    # plt.scatter(   X_[:, x], X_[:, y], alpha=alpha, 
    #                     c=c, cmap="Set1", marker=marker)
    sns.scatterplot(data=None, x=X_[:, x], y=X_[:, y], hue=c)

    # If a pca was provided, compute the % of variance of each axis
    if pca : 
        v1 = str(round(100*pca.explained_variance_ratio_[x]))  + " %"
        v2 = str(round(100*pca.explained_variance_ratio_[y]))  + " %"
    else : 
        v1=v2= ''

    # Axis names, with the percentage of inertia explained
    ax.set_xlabel(f'F{x+1} {v1}')
    ax.set_ylabel(f'F{y+1} {v2}')

    # Max x and y values
    x_max = np.abs(X_[:, x]).max() *1.1
    y_max = np.abs(X_[:, y]).max() *1.1

    # Bound x and y
    ax.set_xlim(left=-x_max, right=x_max)
    ax.set_ylim(bottom= -y_max, top=y_max)

    # Display horizontal and vertical lines
    plt.plot([-x_max, x_max], [0, 0], color='grey', alpha=0.8)
    plt.plot([0,0], [-y_max, y_max], color='grey', alpha=0.8)

    # Display point labels
    if len(labels) : 
        for i,(_x,_y) in enumerate(X_[:,[x,y]]):
            plt.text(_x, _y+0.05, labels[i], fontsize='14', ha='center',va='center') 

    # Title and display
    plt.title(f"Projection des individus (sur F{x+1} et F{y+1})")
    plt.show()

Approach

Exploratory data analysis


3 main topics analyzed:

Out-of-plan usage
Data overconsumption
Data underconsumption

Initial thoughts on characterizing these situations using criteria:

Occasional / Frequent / Regular
Number of months / Average frequency / Number of consecutive months



Scoring methodology

Development of a scoring algorithm per SIM card to identify usage profiles (overconsumption / underconsumption) and automatically recommend the most suitable plan.
Criteria used for the score: - Number of months - Frequency - Last month - Overage day (overconsumption) - Overage proportion (overconsumption) - Underconsumption proportion (underconsumption)

Prototype

Experimentation: - Jupyter as a lab to validate the scoring method - Creation of the plan recommendation method, then verification of its consistency
Flexibility: - All calculation elements are configurable so the algorithm can be adapted to any situation

def calcul_jour_depassement(df_cdr, df_cartessim, dernier_forfait):
    cdr_data = df_cdr.loc[df_cdr['type'] == 'data',['date', 'dataKo', 'iccid']]
    del df_cdr

    # Link with SIM card ids (inner join to exclude unknown iccid)
    sim_iccid = df_cartessim[['_id', 'iccid_text']]
    cdr_data = pd.merge(cdr_data, sim_iccid, left_on='iccid', right_on='iccid_text', how='inner')
    cdr_data = cdr_data[['date', 'dataKo', '_id']]

    # Compute cumulative data consumed per month
    cdr_data = cdr_data.sort_values(['_id', 'date'])
    cdr_data['Mois concerné'] = cdr_data['date'].dt.to_period('M').dt.to_timestamp()
    cdr_data['data_cumsum_ko'] = cdr_data.groupby(['_id', 'Mois concerné'])['dataKo'].cumsum()
    cdr_data.drop(columns='dataKo', inplace=True)
    cdr_data['data_cumsum_go'] = round(cdr_data['data_cumsum_ko'] / config_base.KO_PAR_GO, 2)
    cdr_data.drop(columns='data_cumsum_ko', inplace=True)

    # Link with the plan used (for overconsumption, usage over the whole period is compared to the latest plan, even if the plan changed in the meantime)
    cdr_data = pd.merge(cdr_data, dernier_forfait[['SIM', 'data_go_number']], left_on='_id', right_on='SIM', how='inner')
    cdr_data = cdr_data[['SIM', 'date', 'data_cumsum_go', 'data_go_number']]

    # Flag, then filter rows where cumulative consumption exceeds the plan
    mask = cdr_data['data_cumsum_go'] >= cdr_data['data_go_number'] * config_surconsommation.seuil_surconso
    cdr_data = cdr_data.loc[mask, ['SIM', 'date']]

    # Isolate the day
    cdr_data['jour_depassement'] = cdr_data['date'].dt.day

    # Create overage day df per SIM card (with configured quantile)
    jour_depassement = cdr_data.groupby("SIM")['jour_depassement'].quantile(config_surconsommation.percentile_jour_depassement).reset_index(name="jour_depassement")

    return jour_depassement

title: Business & Technology Watch: Inventory Management Methods
text:
Approach
The goal was to perform targeted business and technology intelligence to improve an existing project:
E-commerce Data Management Optimization.
During that initial project, inventory management issues were highlighted. This watch directly addresses that specific need: Centralize, analyze, and evaluate inventory management methods.
The workflow is structured as follows:

1. Intelligence Gathering

Raw watch data is collected via Feedly by monitoring various relevant inventory management sources.
Whenever an article or resource is deemed relevant, it is saved to the Inventory Management Methods database with one click using the Notion Web Clipper extension.
The entry automatically lands in the list with the status To Summarize.



2. Status Tracking

To Summarize: Article captured, pending in-depth reading and note-taking.
Summarized: Method analyzed, with all evaluation fields completed.
Not Retained: Method analyzed but excluded for this project (reasons documented under Limitations).



3. Processing & Evaluation
Each entry is summarized with the following attributes to evaluate its relevance:

Type: Indicates whether it is a Business method (e.g., Wilson formula) or a Technology method (e.g., Python script).
Description: Concise summary of the article explaining the methodology.
Implementation Difficulty: Low / Medium / High, evaluated based on project constraints.
Reliability: Low / Medium / High, evaluated based on project context.
Limitations: Short overview of the method’s constraints regarding the project.

title: Business & Technology Watch: Inventory Management Methods
text:
Key Results
The output of this watch is a structured Notion database containing all reviewed sources alongside their potential applications within the project. This deliverable was integrated into a comprehensive project framing framework, including a functional specification document, a user guide, and a final summary report.
